clue.text: Artemis confounded these experts

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: The goddess Artemis has baffled a panel of specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural for masters of an art, especially eminent musicians.

clue.text: Adviser putting faulty motion right

indicators.note: something faulty is defective, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A counsellor corrects a badly worded proposal at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor watches over and warns, the role of a counsellor or overseer.

clue.text: Property conveyance?

parts.note: read not as the legal transfer of land but as a vehicle named after a landed holding, a car for the country house

explanation.surface: A conveyancing solicitor's term for transferring a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-backed family vehicle with a rear door is so named, literally a car for an estate.

clue.text: Drink a student calls for-no half measures

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits
L for learner, the plate a student driver displays

explanation.surface: A student orders a drink and insists on a full measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calls for' is a link phrase; L is the learner plate on British cars, a crossword convention for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complete and absolute involves no half measures.

clue.text: Among the expert, a meeting in Africa

parts.note: among can be rendered as in
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: Specialists gather at a conference somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: DAB for an expert comes from the British phrase 'dab hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: An indaba is a Zulu or Xhosa word for a council or important conference in southern Africa.

clue.text: Coaster near to the bar?

parts.note: a coaster here is a small mat for a glass, found in any pub, not a ship sailing close to a sandbar

explanation.surface: A coastal ship sails close to a sandbank at a harbour mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard mat placed under a pint glass in a pub serves as a coaster.

clue.text: Lawyers' stooge gains a seat

parts.note: the Bar is the collective body of barristers
a stool, as in stool pigeon, is a decoy or stooge

explanation.surface: A barrister's lackey gets himself a place to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall seat without a back used at a pub counter.

clue.text: in time ale goes off — get rid of it

indicators.note: goes off suggests beer turning bad, so these letters spoil into a new order

explanation.surface: Beer that sours with age should be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to remove or do away with something completely.

clue.text: In a state of confusion, I enter the plant

indicators.note: enter means go into, so the letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a maze, being in a maze, is a state of bewilderment

explanation.surface: Bewildered, I walk into the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is the cereal crop also called corn.

clue.text: intending to run through?

parts.note: someone meaning to run another through with a blade makes stabbing lunges forward

explanation.surface: A swordsman sets out to pierce an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrusts are sharp forward stabs, the moves of one aiming to skewer a foe.

clue.text: Used system of symbols to sign agreement over the gallery

indicators.note: over here means covering, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to nod is to signal assent
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery's board gives its assent to a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Notated means wrote down, as music, in a set of signs.

clue.text: Climate in Spanish plains fit for a prince?

definitions.text: Climate in Spanish plains fit for a prince?

parts.words: Climate in Spanish plains fit for a prince?
parts.note: recalls the song line that the rain in Spain falls mainly on the plain, giving a wetter climate, while also naming a prince of Monaco

explanation.surface: A weather report on the Spanish plains, worthy of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: From My Fair Lady: 'The rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain'. Prince Rainier III ruled Monaco.
explanation.definitionFit: More wet in comparative form, and also the first name of a twentieth-century prince of Monaco.

clue.text: Angry, sit not at ale bars?

definitions.text: Angry, sit not at ale bars?

indicators.note: an angry state is a disturbed one, so the following letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A grumpy drinker refuses to sit in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Teetotallers are people who never drink alcohol, so would not sit at pub counters.

clue.text: Put spring back and wind up again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to coil is to wind round and round

explanation.surface: A watchmaker refits a mainspring and rewinds it.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to rebound sharply, as a gun does when fired.

clue.text: String-pulling corrupted fine uncle

indicators.note: corrupted means debased or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy relative uses connections for favours.
explanation.definitionFit: Wielding sway behind the scenes is pulling strings.

clue.text: Stays together — it's customary practice in a Greek island

indicators.note: in places the practice inside the island

parts.note: Kos, also spelt Cos, is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
a habit is a customary practice

explanation.surface: Couples living as one is a local tradition on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohabit is to live together as partners without marrying.

clue.text: Initiate reduction with difficulty

indicators.note: suggests the word is forced awkwardly into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bringing in spending cuts proves hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce something is to start or launch it.

clue.text: Aintree toss for second of the apprentices

indicators.note: a toss throws things about, so the racecourse's letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Young jockeys fall at Aintree.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainees are people learning a trade, as apprentices are.

clue.text: About to be hemmed in by herd of stampeding cattle from this place

indicators.note: hemmed in means surrounded, so the earlier pieces go inside the herd

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: a stampede is a wild rush, so the two letters run out of order

explanation.surface: A rancher is trapped by a stampeding herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stampeding' scrambles only the little word 'of'; 'hemmed in by' puts it, after the 'about' piece, inside the herd. Hereford cattle are a red-and-white British beef breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-and-white beef breed is named after the English cathedral city where it originated.

clue.text: In haste, fiery over a measure

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: fiery means hot
a foot is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Rushing with a temper over a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotfoot means hurriedly, at speed.

clue.text: For squashing a cockroach, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a heavy wooden mallet used for pounding and ramming
a common name for a black insect, loosely used for a cockroach

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crushing mallet and a hard-shelled insect.

clue.text: Heavenly in Los Angeles? Yes, could be

indicators.note: could be suggests an alternative form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is paradise found in Hollywood? Possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium was the Greek paradise, so Elysian means blissful or divine.

clue.text: Supplies plants

definitions.meaning: fragrant garden flowers of the genus Matthiola

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both reserves of goods and a type of scented garden flower.

clue.text: No untidy clothes here, for a change

definitions.text: No untidy clothes here, for a change

indicators.note: for a change signals that the letters are swapped into a new form

explanation.surface: A place where people dress neatly, unusually.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist community is where nobody wears clothes at all, so none are untidy.

clue.text: Charming element of the self-indulgent

indicators.note: an element is a part, so the answer lies within the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Something charming in a selfish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means delicately pretty and charming, like a fairy.

clue.text: Embargo dropped — boilerman can provide lubrication

annotationWithheld.why: Embargo dropped — boilerman can provide lubrication: BAN out of BOILERMAN leaves OILERM, not OILER; the hidden reading (bOILERman) leaves 'Embargo dropped' with no job, so the clue as held looks garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Embargo dropped — boilerman can provide lubrication

clue.text: Wrong-doing, to do with a boundary line

parts.note: of means concerning or to do with
a fence marks a boundary

explanation.surface: A trespass case concerning a property line.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a crime or breach of a rule.

clue.text: Stones thrown — I call copper!

indicators.note: thrown suggests things tossed about, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A man hurls rocks and shouts for the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman summoned by the call; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Calculi are hard stone-like masses formed in the body, such as kidney stones.

clue.text: Employed filling in pot holes?

parts.note: suggests road menders, but means travelling menders who patch holes in pots and pans

explanation.surface: Workers patch up road potholes.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant menders of metal pots and kettles were traditionally called this.

clue.text: Boy with inner compulsion to make a career in the theatre

definitions.text: to make a career in the theatre

indicators.note: with inner means having something inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a son is a boy
an urge is a compulsion

explanation.surface: A young man feels a drive to become an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who operates works in an operating theatre.
